title: 391. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Nets of Three-Dimensional Solids
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Face count in a cube net
questions.learningObjective: Count the square faces needed for a closed cube net.
questions.question: A net of a closed cube contains exactly one square for each face, with no tabs or overlaps. How many squares does it contain?
questions.explanation: A closed cube has three pairs of opposite square faces, for a total of \(6\). A five-square layout leaves one face missing.
questions.hint: Account for each pair of opposite faces.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the rectangle dimensions in a right-cylinder net.
questions.question: A closed right circular cylinder has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and height \(7\text{ cm}\). What are the dimensions of the rectangular part of its net?
questions.explanation: One dimension wraps once around the base circumference, \(2\pi(2)=4\pi\text{ cm}\). The other is the height, \(7\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Determine the distance that must wrap around a full circular base.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the sector radius and arc length in a cone net.
questions.question: A right circular cone has base radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(5\text{ cm}\). What are the radius and arc length of its lateral sector net?

options.label: A
options.text: Sector radius \(3\text{ cm}\), arc length \(10\pi\text{ cm}\)

options.label: B
options.text: Sector radius \(5\text{ cm}\), arc length \(6\pi\text{ cm}\)

questions.explanation: The sector radius is the slant height, \(5\text{ cm}\). Its arc wraps around the base, so the arc length is \(2\pi(3)=6\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Match radial distances and boundary lengths between the cone and its unfolded surface.

questions.concept: Face types in a rectangular-prism net
questions.learningObjective: Identify the required pairs of rectangular faces.
questions.question: A closed rectangular prism has edge lengths \(2\), \(3\), and \(5\). Which collection of rectangles must its net contain?
questions.explanation: Each pair of edge directions defines a pair of opposite faces. The three face sizes are \(2\)-by-\(3\), \(2\)-by-\(5\), and \(3\)-by-\(5\), each appearing twice.
questions.hint: Pair the edge lengths to identify the three opposite-face pairs.

questions.concept: Triangle area in a pyramid net
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the height of a triangular face in a pyramid net.
questions.question: A regular square pyramid has base side \(6\text{ cm}\) and face slant height \(4\text{ cm}\), measured from the apex to an edge midpoint. What is the area of each triangular piece in its net?
questions.explanation: Each piece is a triangle with base \(6\) and in-face perpendicular height \(4\). Its area is \(\frac{1}{2}(6)(4)=12\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Use the triangular face's altitude, not the pyramid's vertical height.

questions.learningObjective: Match a prism's lateral and base faces to its net.
questions.question: A right prism has equilateral triangular bases of side \(4\) and lateral edges of length \(9\). Which face collection is required in its net?

options.label: A
options.text: Three \(4\)-by-\(9\) rectangles and two equilateral triangles of side \(4\)

options.label: B
options.text: Four \(4\)-by-\(9\) rectangles and one equilateral triangle of side \(4\)

questions.explanation: Each of the three base edges generates one rectangle, and the closed prism has two triangular bases. The net therefore requires exactly these five faces.
questions.hint: Count the lateral faces from the number of base edges.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a valid cube net from a straight strip.
questions.question: Unit squares are specified by their lower-left grid coordinates and joined along common edges. Which arrangement folds into a cube without overlap?
questions.explanation: In the flapped-strip layout, the four-square strip forms the side faces and the two flaps close opposite ends. A six-square straight strip repeats face positions after four successive right-angle folds, causing overlap.
questions.hint: Track the face directions after folding adjacent squares through right angles.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why face count alone does not certify a cube net.
questions.question: Six unit squares fill a complete \(2\)-by-\(3\) rectangle, joined along every shared edge. Can this layout fold into a cube without cutting any joins or overlapping faces?
questions.explanation: At an interior grid vertex, four squares are joined cyclically. Folding all their shared edges as cube edges is inconsistent: a cube vertex has only three incident faces. The intact rectangular layout is therefore not a cube net.
questions.hint: Examine the number of joined squares around an interior grid vertex.

questions.concept: Disk radius from a cylinder net
questions.learningObjective: Recover a base radius from the wrapping rectangle width.
questions.question: A closed cylinder's net has a lateral rectangle of dimensions \(12\pi\text{ cm}\) by \(10\text{ cm}\). The \(12\pi\text{ cm}\) side wraps around the base. What is the radius of each circular piece?
questions.explanation: The wrapping length equals circumference, so \(2\pi r=12\pi\). Thus each base disk has radius \(6\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Equate the specified wrapping side to the circle's circumference.

questions.concept: Base radius from a cone's sector angle
questions.learningObjective: Convert a cone net's sector arc length into base radius.
questions.question: A sector of radius \(12\text{ cm}\) and angle \(150^\circ\) forms a cone's curved surface with no overlap. What radius must the circular base piece have?
questions.explanation: The sector arc is \(\frac{150}{360}(2\pi\cdot12)=10\pi\text{ cm}\). Equating this to \(2\pi r\) gives \(r=5\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Compute the sector arc before matching it to the base circumference.
